originality.rationale: The novelty claim is restricted to the simultaneous full Frobenius cycle table of three naturally attached finite étale schemes, the constituent-line refinement, and the sharp rational-plane descent boundary. The classical 27-line and 45-plane incidence, specific involution counts, and the broader Galois-class statistical methods are expressly treated as prior art. Comparison of available primary text and nearby recorded findings did not identify this complete combined table. This is a best-knowledge assessment with the important residual risk that existing general character-theory machinery may imply it.
residual_risks: Das (2020) and earlier W(E6) character-class methods may imply the new finite table without expressly printing it; originality is priority-provisional rather than logically independent of known machinery.
Unindexed historical books, computational appendices or additional character tables could contain matching cycle data; a negative search is not proof of novelty.
Relevant indexed result summaries outside primary literature were compared at summary level only; full documents were not all inspected.
All geometric realization claims are conditional; not every partition is proved realizable over every individual finite field.

value.rationale: The 27-line/45-plane/135-flag finite étale data are canonical for a marked cubic surface and encode field-of-definition information of both configurations and their incidences. The complete eleven-type orbit census determines all extension-field counts and zeta factors, while the rational-plane 0/1/3-component classification isolates natural descent obstructions, especially the (6) and (3,3) cases with planes but no rational lines. This supplies an exact natural arithmetic invariant missing from the inspected explicit statistics, rather than an arbitrary numerical test.
